A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the immunological properties of link protein are different from those of the hyaluronate-binding subunits of proteoglycan and that the link protein subunit is immunologically distinguishable from the hyaluronidase-sensitive region of monomer.
link protein is an immunologically distinct molecular species which is a subunit of the proteoglycan molecule.

link protein is a distinct molecular species in cartilage, that it is immunologically unrelated to proteoglycans and to type II collagen, and that it is a dimeric species composed of immunologically distinguishable subunits.
The main takeaway from our work is that

link protein is immunologically distinct from proteoglycan and collagen, and that the link region of proteoglycan is antigenically distinct from the chondroitin sulfate and keratan sulfate chains of proteoglycans.
the link protein of bovine nasal cartilages is not identical to the link protein of adult bovine artifular and foetal bovine nasal cartiles.

link protein can be isolated from bovine nasal proteochondroitin sulphate in high yields, that it is a glycoprotein, that it contains two immunologically distinct species, that it binds to the hyaluronate region of proteochondroitin sulfate monomer, and that it is a component of the chondroitin sulfate-rich matrix of cartilage.
